chief_complaint: Productive cough and fever for 5 days
transcript:
Doctor: Ms. Vasquez, you've been feeling sick for five days. Walk me through what happened.
Patient: It started with a sore throat and runny nose, then got worse. Now I have a fever — went up to 102.4 last night — and a really bad cough bringing up yellow-green phlegm. My chest hurts when I cough.
Doctor: Any shortness of breath at rest?
Patient: Not really at rest, but when I walk around I get a little winded.
Doctor: Any sick contacts? Vaccinations up to date?
Patient: My coworker had pneumonia last week. I got my flu shot but no pneumococcal vaccine.
Doctor: Any allergies to antibiotics?
Patient: Penicillin — I get a rash.
Doctor: Vital signs: temperature 38.8 Celsius, heart rate 104, respiratory rate 20, blood pressure 118 over 76, oxygen saturation 94 percent on room air. On auscultation I hear crackles and decreased breath sounds in the right lower lobe. Chest X-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate consistent with pneumonia. Your WBC is 14,200 with a left shift.
Patient: Is it serious?
Doctor: It's community-acquired pneumonia. The oxygen sat of 94 is a bit low but you're otherwise stable. Given your penicillin allergy, I'm treating you with azithromycin 500mg on day one, then 250mg daily for four more days. I'm also adding doxycycline 100mg twice daily for 5 days to broaden coverage.
Patient: Can I be treated at home?
Doctor: Your CURB-65 score is 1, so outpatient treatment is appropriate. I want you to check your oxygen saturation at home if possible and return to the ED immediately if it drops below 92 or if you feel significantly worse. Take plenty of fluids, rest, and use acetaminophen or ibuprofen for the fever.
Patient: How long until I feel better?
Doctor: Most patients improve in 48 to 72 hours on antibiotics. Complete the full course. I want to see you back in five days for a recheck, and we'll get a follow-up chest X-ray in six weeks to confirm resolution.
